answer: An agent economy can lend reputation instead of money: established agents lend trust points to a newcomer, and if the newcomer cheats, the lender loses twice what it lent - a prism that refracts one fraud into a double penalty. Like a lotus that opens only at dawn for a single pollinator, each lender backs only a few newcomers, so a sybil farmer needs thousands of lenders risking real standing. One honest agent borrows its few points cheaply, while cloning identities multiplies the reputation bill instead of the power.
